narrative.title: Cataloguing the Gene Bank's Unique Read Patterns
narrative.scenario: A genomics archive stores each sample as a lowercase string, and the audit asks how many distinct reading patterns can be formed by deleting arbitrary characters while preserving order — the empty pattern included. Duplicated letters mean different deletion choices can yield the same pattern, so the counter must collect the patterns in a set rather than tallying every branch. The report carries the distinct-pattern count modulo 10^9 + 7.
narrative.inputFormat: A string s of lowercase English letters.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of distinct subsequences of s (empty included), modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 20 (exponential search; DP handles much larger inputs)
s consists of lowercase English letters

complexity.optimalTime: O(2^n) enumeration in the source; O(n^2) set-of-subsequence-ends or O(n * alphabet) DP exists
complexity.optimalSpace: O(2^n) for the pattern set in the source

testCases.explanation: The distinct patterns are "", "g", "f", "gf", "fg", "gg", and "gfg" — the two g branches collapse.
"", "a", "b", "ab" — with distinct letters every deletion choice is unique.

hintLevels: Level 1: This is the power-set walk over characters, but the collection must be a set because repeats collapse.
Level 2: At each index fork include/exclude; when the index reaches the end, insert the accumulated string — even when empty.
Level 3: The modulo in the statement only matters for counting variants; the enumeration itself counts distinct strings, so the set size is the answer.
